[EFFECT]
Wind speed has almost no effect on predicted demand when winds are calm to moderate (up to roughly 20 km/h, or a normalised value of about 0.3), where the contribution hovers near zero with a very slight positive nudge at the lowest speeds. Beyond that threshold, higher wind speeds progressively reduce predicted demand, with the contribution falling to around −0.33 at the strongest observed winds (about 55 km/h). The shape is essentially flat at low speeds, then steadily and noticeably negative from moderate speeds onward.

[IMPORTANCE]
Windspeed is ranked 8th out of 9 features in terms of overall importance (importance score = 0.014), making it one of the weakest drivers of predicted demand. Its influence only becomes meaningful at higher wind speeds.

[RECOMMENDATION]
On days forecast to have strong winds (above roughly 20 km/h), consider slightly reducing the number of bikes deployed or staff scheduled, as demand is expected to drop — the stronger the wind, the larger the expected reduction.
